observations: Photos show a vehicle drivetrain assembly that appears to include a gearbox/transmission (large metal transmission case) with attached components and wiring/hoses.
No clear readable brand/model markings are visible on the transmission case in the provided photos.
The assembly looks used and disassembled/removed (loose hoses/wiring, surrounding drivetrain parts in frame).
Seller text claims Jeep Wrangler 3.6L 2011 4X4 and “direct America drive” / “direct from Belgium”, but these are not verifiable from the photos shown.

claims.evidence: Photos do not show a readable Jeep/Wrangler/3.6L/2011 identification tag or part number.
No odometer/vehicle history or label is visible in the photos.
No shipping/import documents or markings are visible in the photos.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: Photos show a removed/used transmission assembly but do not show a test run, diagnostic printout, or seal/inspection evidence to confirm 'never opened' or 'no knock'.

risks.risk: Wrong transmission fitment (Wrangler 3.6L 2011 4x4 can have different transmission variants; mismatch will waste money and time).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the transmission ID/part number label and/or stamped code on the case (and the matching VIN/vehicle spec the seller used).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst case: not confirmed correct fitment (treated like a generic used gearbox with unknown compatibility).

risks.risk: Not actually working / internal damage (seller says tested, but photos can’t confirm).
risks.proof: Video clip of the gearbox being engaged/operated on a test rig (or proof of bench test) showing smooth engagement in all gears.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst case: not working / needs overhaul.

risks.risk: “Never opened” may be false; seals/gaskets could have been replaced or internals previously repaired.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of case seams, bolts, and any sealant lines; plus a photo of the transmission pan/cover area if applicable.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst case: unknown history (treated like previously opened/overhauled risk).

risks.proof: Any label showing mileage/vehicle source, or import/auction paperwork; otherwise a test/inspection report.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst case: mileage unknown (treated as average-wear used unit).

risks.risk: Missing accessories/transfer case components (seller may be selling only part of what’s needed for Wrangler 4x4).
risks.proof: A full photo inventory laid out (what’s included: transmission only vs transmission+transfer case, sensors, torque converter/flexplate items, mounts, wiring harness connectors).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worst case: transmission only, missing some required parts.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the transmission ID/part number label or stamped code on the gearbox case (the exact code that matches Wrangler 3.6L 2011 4x4).
Video of the gearbox being tested (engagement through gears / reverse) or a bench-test report showing it works and no abnormal noise.
Photos showing whether the unit has been opened before: case seam/bolt heads/any sealant marks; plus close-ups of seals/gaskets.
A photo list of exactly what is included in the sale (transmission only vs transmission + transfer case + sensors + mounts + required connectors).
response.reason: The photos show a used transmission assembly, but they do not provide readable identification or test proof to confirm the exact Wrangler 3.6L 2011 4x4 fitment and working condition. Without that, a reliable worst-case price pick from comparables isn’t safe.
